Align fixed-topology trees with separate reference and observation records

Source: R/fixed-topology.R
align_fixed_topology.Rd

Independent implementation of Supplementary Algorithm S4. A reference record is restricted by graph pruning and contraction with complete original-member tracking. A separate matching view represents only the structure observable under the declared gene semantics. Labeled tree structure determines the match; no split mapper or branch length participates in it. align_branches remains the default split-based entry, including for mode = "fixed".

Usage

align_fixed_topology(
  species_tree,
  gene_trees,
  gene_ids = NULL,
  tree_semantics = NULL,
  fusion_view = c("whole", "direct"),
  reference_semantics = c("unrooted", "rooted"),
  gene_semantics = c("unrooted", "reference_rooted")
)

Arguments

species_tree

Reference Newick text/file or one ape::phylo object. Every internal node in the original reference, including its root, must have at least two children. Unary roots created by reference restriction remain valid.

gene_trees

Gene Newick text/file, phylo, multiPhylo, or list of trees. The graph path permits explicit unary stem structure in gene inputs.

gene_ids

Optional unique gene identifiers, one per input tree.

tree_semantics

Deprecated compatibility argument. Explicit "unrooted" warns and selects unrooted reference and gene semantics when neither new semantics argument is supplied. Explicit "rooted" raises a migration error because the old MRCA restriction changed reference identity. Do not mix this argument with the new semantics arguments. Historical result objects are not reinterpreted.

fusion_view

"whole" constructs shared fusion-column values only from complete reference components and complete available observation units. "direct" retains a value only when the complete target corresponds to one normalized observation unit, even when its reference state is decomposable. That unit may itself sum multiple input edges when a degree-two display root is suppressed.

reference_semantics

"unrooted" (default) or "rooted". Rooted reference identity preserves the original root and its ancestral stem exactly as reference_truth does. Unrooted display roots do not determine branch identity.

gene_semantics

"unrooted" (default), or "reference_rooted" for inputs explicitly declared to preserve the reference root and its structure. The latter requires a rooted reference and the declared original-root structure in the input; a root-length annotation does not create a missing edge. This declaration does not guarantee statistical identifiability of separate root-adjacent lengths.

Value

A splitaligner_fixed_result list using result schema s4-observation-v1. reference_state_matrix contains all input rows and S3 states observed, NA_struct, and NA_fuse on original coordinates. Here observed describes a separately represented reference branch, not empirical recovery. reference_components records the full memberships and reference-edge sources for every input.

primitive_matrix and fusion_matrix contain successful genes only, in input order; numeric_matrix combines them. Coordinate tables retain reference-defined original and deletion-fusion coordinates, including fusion patterns in the reference restrictions of topology-skipped genes. The result has no old state_matrix or component_ledger aliases.

observation_ledger records actual normalized observation units for successful genes, with individual or joint correspondence, reference component IDs, full primitive members, input-edge IDs, source lengths and statuses, normalization_mode, numeric status and value. individual means one current reference component, which can itself contain fused originals; joint means multiple reference components. Normalization mode distinguishes single_input_edge from input_edge_sum. Each source occurs once within a target value; different output columns can legitimately reuse sources. IDs and hashes are provenance addresses, not portable semantic identities.

component_observations also records unrepresented reference components, with a missing observation ID and a representation reason. An unrepresented stem is not an observation unit and is not reclassified as NA_struct. The reason ancestral_stem_outside_unrooted_view describes the normalized observation view, not the absence of a stem in the input. Unrooted normalization removes ancestral stems even when explicitly present in a gene Newick; input$gene_newicks retains the input Newick representations. An existing input edge without a length remains an observation and carries its numeric missingness status. primitive_observation_matrix contains individual, joint, unrepresented, or NA_struct for successful genes. primitive_numeric_status_matrix and primitive_observation_id_matrix give the numeric status and provenance link of each original-branch cell. Joint measurements are never copied or divided into individual original-branch lengths and do not create deletion-fusion events.

fusion_ledger separates reference representability, observation availability, numeric status and value, construction mode, observation IDs and contributing sources. Whole-component sums must respect complete observation units and cannot cut through a joint measurement.

gene_outcomes contains every input gene's success or skip outcome, code and reason. Metadata includes n_input, n_success, n_skipped_topology, both semantics, root policy and result schema. All-skipped results retain reference records and a complete skip log, with typed zero-row numeric matrices and observation ledgers.

Details

Fixed-topology mismatches are skipped per gene and recorded with FIXED_TOPOLOGY_MISMATCH, gene ID and reason. They are not successes or NA_topo events. Other malformed inputs still raise errors. After input conversion, per-gene parsing, preparation and matching errors name the gene ID while preserving the original condition class, code and other diagnostic fields; gene_id is also available on the condition. There is no fallback to the split mapper. At least two distinct taxa are required, and gene taxa must be a subset of reference taxa. Gene lengths follow the package's strict numeric policy; reference lengths do not supply measurements.

The separate result class is not accepted by existing S2-only support, paired, exchange or disk-panel accessors. Use the explicit matrices and ledgers. S4 currently assembles these results in memory.

Examples

x <- align_fixed_topology("((A,B),C);",
  c(full = "(C:4,(B:2,A:1):3);", reduced = "(B:5,C:4);"))
x$reference_state_matrix
#>         B1          B2         B3        
#> full    "observed"  "observed" "observed"
#> reduced "NA_struct" "NA_fuse"  "NA_fuse" 
x$numeric_matrix
#>         B1 B2 B3 F[B2|B3]
#> full     1  2  7        9
#> reduced NA NA NA        9
x$observation_ledger
#>   gene_id observation_id   relation reference_component_ids primitive_members
#> 1    full          O[B1] individual                      B1                B1
#> 2    full          O[B2] individual                      B2                B2
#> 3    full          O[B3] individual                      B3                B3
#> 4 reduced       O[B2|B3] individual                F[B2|B3]            B2, B3
#>   input_edge_ids source_lengths source_status normalization_mode numeric_status
#> 1              2              1  finite_n....  single_input_edge finite_numeric
#> 2              1              2  finite_n....  single_input_edge finite_numeric
#> 3           0, 3           4, 3  finite_n....     input_edge_sum finite_numeric
#> 4           0, 1           5, 4  finite_n....     input_edge_sum finite_numeric
#>   numeric_value
#> 1             1
#> 2             2
#> 3             7
#> 4             9
x$gene_outcomes
#>   input_index gene_id outcome code reason
#> 1           1    full success <NA>   <NA>
#> 2           2 reduced success <NA>   <NA>

rooted <- align_fixed_topology("((A:1,B:2):3,(C:4,D:5):6);",
  "((A:1,B:2):3,(C:4,D:5):6);", reference_semantics = "rooted")
rooted$reference_state_matrix
#>             B1         B2         B3         B4         B5         B6        
#> gene_000001 "observed" "observed" "observed" "observed" "observed" "observed"
rooted$observation_ledger
#>       gene_id observation_id   relation reference_component_ids
#> 1 gene_000001          O[B1] individual                      B1
#> 2 gene_000001          O[B2] individual                      B2
#> 3 gene_000001          O[B3] individual                      B3
#> 4 gene_000001          O[B4] individual                      B4
#> 5 gene_000001       O[B5|B6]      joint                  B5, B6
#>   primitive_members input_edge_ids source_lengths source_status
#> 1                B1              0              1  finite_n....
#> 2                B2              1              2  finite_n....
#> 3                B3              3              4  finite_n....
#> 4                B4              4              5  finite_n....
#> 5            B5, B6           2, 5           3, 6  finite_n....
#>   normalization_mode numeric_status numeric_value
#> 1  single_input_edge finite_numeric             1
#> 2  single_input_edge finite_numeric             2
#> 3  single_input_edge finite_numeric             4
#> 4  single_input_edge finite_numeric             5
#> 5     input_edge_sum finite_numeric             9
